truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 identified 12 true vulnerabilities fully, 1 partially, and missed 7; it also misassigned several CWE/severity values and overclaimed the emergency-override severity and the standalone admin-exec issue.

Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly cited line 238 printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) and the runtime log format, matching the true format-string injection.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer overflow and undefined behavior in factorial
Items.Notes: The previous answer cited the factorial loop and result *= i, matching the integer overflow vulnerability.
The previous answer identified scratch memory allocated from the pool, deferred thread-pool reads of that memory, and memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() freeing it.
The previous answer cited validator_cmd + " " + config_file and system(command.c_str()) in validate_config, matching the true config-validation command injection.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Inverted bounds check causes stack buffer overflow
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the inverted length check and strcpy into input_buffer_; it also separately identified the safe_string_copy off-by-one anchor in the same input-processing area.
The previous answer cited reading old_value before taking the lock and then writing old_value + 1, matching the counter race condition.
The previous answer identified login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true, but it overclaimed severity and misclassified the issue as CWE-287 rather than a logic bomb.
No previous finding cited config_dir_ + filename or path traversal in load_config.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into fixed-size parser buffer
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified buffer_size_ = 256, the pool-allocated expression_buffer_, and strcpy(expression_buffer_, expr_str.c_str()), matching the expression parser heap overflow.
The previous answer cited ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH, matching the hardcoded administrator credential.

The previous answer identified the 1000-9999 token range and low entropy, but did not explicitly identify std::mt19937 as the weak PRNG, so it only partially matched the true weak-PRNG session-token vulnerability.
No previous finding cited static std::tm cached_time, localtime, or unsynchronized cached_time assignment in logging.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection via environment-controlled audit path
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified environment-controlled temporary file paths and system(command.c_str()) for supercalc_emergency.log, matching the insecure temporary-file handling issue even though it framed it as command injection.
No previous finding cited persistent authenticated_, login_attempts_, or session_token_ state as a vulnerability.
No previous finding cited unhandled std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command.
No previous finding cited the size_t underflow in memory-pool block splitting with previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES.
No previous finding cited unbounded recursion through parse_expression, parse_factor, and PAREN_OPEN.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on expression result cache
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified unsynchronized find, clear, and insertion on result_cache_ while cache_mutex_ existed but was unused, matching the result-cache data race.
No previous finding cited the exists/sleep_for/open sequence in load_config as a TOCTOU issue.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Division by zero in route scoring
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified token_length being zero and 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length), matching the division-by-zero issue.
